audit_findings.title: Asset retirement obligations of $8.4bn are a senior claim absent from both owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $8,364M ARO plus $220M accrued environmental = $8,584M, or $7.10/share on 1,209.708M shares — 12.0% of the base value of $58.98/share. Related filed figures: 2025 ARO accretion $366M (income-statement accretion on discounted liabilities $378M), ARO cash spending $259M, balance up from $8,215M to $8,364M.
audit_findings.mechanism: Bridge: equity value = operating PV + stakes + cash − debt. The bridge carries stakes 0.0, cash 7,692 and debt 23,290 marked CONTEXT_ONLY_NOT_DEDUCTED, so no ARO line exists anywhere. In owner earnings, the offsetting risk is that non-cash accretion is added back while only $259M of cash settlement is charged.
audit_findings.evidence: Most of these obligations are not expected to be paid until several years, or decades, in the future and will be funded from general company resources at the time of removal.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission from the bridge is demonstrated on the face of the valuation record — ARO simply is not a line in it. Whether it is also an error is a doctrine question the record does not settle: debt is excluded deliberately because equity-level OE retains interest expense, but ARO has no equivalent charge running through earnings, so the same reasoning does not transfer to it. The filing is explicit that these obligations are settled 'from general company resources at the time of removal', which is the definition of a claim ahead of the common. At $7.10/share this is material to the computed intrinsic value; it does not change the buy/no-buy conclusion, since the price of $135.72 is already 3.3x the buy-below of $41.29, and the effect pushes value further down.
audit_findings.action: Pull the 4b extraction worksheet for FY2025 and establish two things: whether the $366M/$378M accretion was added back, and whether ARO settlement spending sits inside the maintenance-capex deduction. Then get a PIPELINE.md ruling on whether ARO belongs in the bridge as a deduction alongside debt-treatment policy, and if so re-run 4d with the deduction. Note the unreconciled starting point: FY2025 CFO $19,796M less capex and investments $12,553M is $7,243M, against an anchor of $4,789M — a $2,454M gap the supplied record does not explain.

audit_findings.title: $23bn of post-2031 LNG take-or-pay obligations sit outside the anchor year almost entirely
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed fixed and determinable payments: 2026 $7M; 2027 $7M; 2028 $397M; 2029 $558M; 2030 $602M; 2031 and after $23bn. Total contractual purchase obligations $44,977M, of which LNG offtake, regasification and vessels $29,722M. Total payments under these agreements were $25M in 2025. Approximately $1bn of undiscounted payments for time-chartered LNG vessels not yet commenced at 31-Dec-2025; the Q2-2026 10-Q adds roughly $7bn more of LNG offtake, vessel and capacity obligations. The offsetting sales leg is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Anchor level (FY2025 OE carries $25M of a cost structure that steps up inside and beyond the forecast window) and, for the vessel commitments, potentially the bridge as a fixed claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The fixed and determinable portion of the remaining estimated payments under these various agreements as of December 31, 2025 is: 2026—$ 7 million; 2027—$ 7 million; 2028—$ 397 million; 2029—$ 558 million; 2030—$ 602 million; and 2031 and after—$ 23 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The asymmetry is real and filed: the take-or-pay legs are fixed and the sales legs are not, and the anchor carries essentially none of the future cost. But materiality cannot be established from the record, because the same contracts bring volumes and margin that are equally absent from the anchor — the net effect could go either way, and the filing's statement that purchases are 'expected to be offset in the same or approximately same periods by cash received from the related sales transactions' is an expectation, not a contractual match. One correction to the finding: the supplied valuation record contains no LNG-specific bull rationale — bull is a generic +5% growth band — so the claim that the bull case is built explicitly on the 10.2 to 12.2 MTPA expansion is not supported by the record under review.
audit_findings.action: Do not adjust the anchor on this. Record it as a forecast-window structural change and revisit at the next refresh, when 2028-2030 payments ($397M/$558M/$602M) begin appearing in actuals and a realised LNG margin can be observed. Separately, get a ruling on whether the ~$1bn of undiscounted payments for time-chartered vessels not yet commenced is a bridge claim under the same policy that governs operating leases (currently context, not deducted, at $950M).

audit_findings.title: Perimeter ruled unchanged although Marathon lands mid-series and a $5bn disposal programme is live
audit_findings.magnitude: Marathon closed 22-Nov-2024: $24,215M of net PP&E acquired, total production 2,375 MBOED in 2025 versus 1,987 MBOED in 2024, +20% headline and +2.5% after adjusting for closed acquisitions and dispositions. Disposals: $3.2bn closed in 2025 (Lower 48 assets sold in 2025 averaged approximately 33 MBOED in 2024); a further $1.7bn signed in Q2-2026 and closed Q3-2026, on assets that averaged approximately 21 MBOED in 2025 — about 0.9% of total production.
audit_findings.mechanism: Anchor comparability across the nine-year OE series (which feeds the trend test and the TOO_HARD evidence) and, prospectively, the level the 2% base growth is applied to.
audit_findings.evidence: In August 2025, we announced a total disposition target of $5 billion by year-end 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: Two separable issues sit inside this finding and they do not carry the same weight. The forward shrinkage is small: the assets still leaving the perimeter produced roughly 21 MBOED, under one percent of output, so growing the FY2025 anchor at 2% is not meaningfully overstated on that account, and the $5bn target has now been met. The series break is not small: Marathon is a 20% production step landing between FY2024 and FY2025, which means the too_hard_reason's comparison of FY2022's $14,817M against FY2025's $4,789M spans materially different asset bases and overstates the like-for-like decline. Since the anchor rule took the latest actual rather than a trend, the anchor level itself is not corrupted by this; the growth judgment and the TOO_HARD narrative are. That the perimeter test returned null while an announced, partly executed $5bn disposal programme was live is a process gap worth fixing regardless of the small dollar effect.
audit_findings.action: Re-run the 4c perimeter test with a rule that flags completed acquisitions and dispositions inside the series window, not only pending ones, and obtain a P1-P4 ruling on the Marathon step. Re-state the growth reasoning on a like-for-like basis using the filing's own adjusted-production figures (2025 +2.5% after acquisitions and dispositions) rather than the headline series, and re-check whether the TOO_HARD conclusion survives that restatement.

audit_findings.title: A perpetual terminal value is fitted to a reserve base the company is not replacing
audit_findings.magnitude: Terminal value is 49.0% of base operating PV of $63,662M, roughly $31,194M or $25.79/share of the $58.98 base value; 45.6% in bear and 50.9% in bull. Reserve life: 7,637 MMBOE total proved against 877 MMBOE of 2025 production, 8.7 years (consolidated 6,506 against 796, 8.2 years). Reserve replacement 80% in 2025 (99% organic); 145% over three years (106% organic). PUDs are 37% of total proved. Future development costs in the standardized measure: $42,794M consolidated plus $3,175M for equity affiliates.
audit_findings.mechanism: Terminal value construction: the business-default fade to 2.5% and a perpetuity at 10% minus 2.5% applied to a depleting reserve base, with maintenance capex set at a level that produced 80% replacement in the anchor year.
audit_findings.evidence: Our reserve replacement was 80 percent in 2025, reflecting a net decrease from dispositions in noncore assets in Lower 48 and lower prices, partially offset by development drilling activity and extensions and discoveries.
audit_findings.explanation: This is the largest single structural exposure in the valuation: about half of computed value sits in a perpetuity for an asset base whose proved reserve life is under nine years and whose 2025 replacement was 80%. The finding overstates the case slightly — a proved reserve base is an SEC-defined subset priced at 12-month averages, and three-year replacement was 145% (106% organic), so the business plainly does replace reserves rather than running to zero. But that is precisely the point in dispute: a 2.5% perpetual growth rate presumes replacement above 100% funded from a maintenance-capex figure that in the anchor year delivered 80%. Either the capex charged in the anchor is too low for the terminal assumption, or the terminal assumption is too generous for the capex charged. The pipeline applied the business default without testing whether an E&P has a terminal state at all.
audit_findings.action: Get a PIPELINE.md ruling on terminal treatment for E&P names — a reserve-run-off or finite-life tail versus the business-default 2.5% perpetuity — and re-run 4d under both to bound the value. In the same pass, test the anchor's maintenance capex against reserve-replacement adequacy: with 37% of proved reserves undeveloped and $42.8bn of future development cost in the standardized measure, establish whether the capex deducted in the anchor is consistent with holding production flat, let alone growing it at 2.5% forever.

audit_findings.title: Roughly $1.4bn of non-recurring benefits are retained inside the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: The 2025 portion is approximately $0.9bn, not $1.4bn: of the ~$1bn of one-time Marathon benefits, $0.5bn was recognised on close in Q4-2024 (Corporate and Other cites the absence in 2025 of a $455M/$394M 2024 foreign-tax-credit benefit), leaving the NOL cash tax benefits 'most of which was recognized in 2025' plus a separate approximately $0.4bn OBBBA cash tax benefit recognised in 2025. That is 18.8% of the $4,789M anchor. Offsetting: $286M of restructuring severance ($214M in production and operating expenses, $72M in SG&A), a genuine one-off cost, roughly 6.0%. Net overstatement approximately $0.6bn, 12.5% of the anchor.
audit_findings.mechanism: Anchor level. Value scales close to linearly with the anchor: a 12.5% lower anchor gives operating PV of roughly $55.7bn and $52.41/share; the gross 18.8% adjustment gives roughly $49.09/share, against the computed $58.98.
audit_findings.evidence: In the first half of 2025, we completed the asset integration of Marathon Oil and by year-end 2025 achieved more than $1 billion of synergies on a run-rate basis and approximately $1 billion of one-time benefits.
audit_findings.explanation: The direction and rough size are established from filed figures, and a $6 to $10 per share swing on a $58.98 base is material to the computed value even though it does not change the conclusion at a price of $135.72. Two components of the finding are unresolved rather than wrong. The $731M before-tax disposition gain is reversed inside operating cash flow, so if the OE build starts from CFO it is already out and charging it again would double-count; if the build starts from net income it may still be in. And the $286M severance cuts the other way, so the net figure depends on whether the extraction normalised it. The absence of a stated reconciliation for the anchor year is the real defect here — the record as supplied cannot show which of these four items was adjusted.
audit_findings.action: Retrieve the 4b FY2025 extraction and its proposed/judged JSON, and confirm the treatment of all four items: the ~$0.5bn NOL cash tax benefit, the ~$0.4bn OBBBA benefit, the $731M disposition gain and the $286M severance. Re-derive the anchor with each normalised and re-run 4d; report the resulting value_ps alongside the current $58.98. While in the worksheet, reconcile the $2,454M gap between FY2025 CFO less capex ($19,796M − $12,553M = $7,243M) and the $4,789M anchor — that gap may already account for some of these items.

audit_findings.title: $8.8bn of equity affiliates is valued at zero in the bridge while their construction funding is charged against owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Equity investments $8,833M at 31-Dec-2025 ($8,980M at 30-Jun-2026). Pre-production carrying value: PALNG approximately $1.6bn, plus NFE4 and NFS3 inside the approximately $1.7bn Qatar total (which also contains producing N3), so roughly $2.5bn to $3.3bn — $2.07 to $2.73 per share. Approximately $0.5bn of 2025 capital expenditures and investments went to NFE4, NFS3 and PALNG, about 10% of the $4,789M anchor. Producing affiliates distributed $1,531M in 2025 against $1,335M of equity earnings.
audit_findings.mechanism: Anchor (if the $0.5bn of pre-production construction spend sits inside the capex deducted from OE) and bridge (stakes_net is 0.0 against $8,833M of equity investments, with step 3 auto-skipped).
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the carrying value of our equity method investment in PALNG was approximately $ 1.6 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The asymmetry described is coherent and would understate value if it holds: the owner is charged for building assets that are credited nowhere. But the finding is conditional on a fact the supplied record does not establish — whether the maintenance-capex deduction in the anchor includes the equity-LNG investments. The $2,454M gap between FY2025 CFO less capex and the anchor means the build cannot be reconstructed from what is here. The finding is also right to limit the claim to pre-production stakes: APLNG at approximately $4.9bn and N3 distribute cash that flows through OE, so crediting their carrying value in the bridge as well would double-count. Correctly scoped, this is worth roughly $2 to $3 per share of bridge credit plus up to a 10% uplift to the anchor — not trivial, but conditional.
audit_findings.action: Read the 4b capex derivation and determine whether the $0.5bn of equity-method LNG investments is inside the deduction. If it is, apply one remedy and only one: either exclude that growth spend from the anchor, or run step 3 to book the pre-production stakes (PALNG, NFE4, NFS3) at carrying value in the bridge while explicitly excluding APLNG and N3, whose distributions already reach OE. If it is not inside the deduction, close the finding with that reconciliation recorded.
